requirements.text: David Ramirez has raised a critical incident to address a severe network issue ... high urgency due to the high business impact
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_018' AND status = 'new' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest on the seed is INC_100); the only incident the task creates
caller_id added to the benchmark check: David Ramirez is USER_018 on the seed (the only David Ramirez; active, a reporter)
status = new from policy 3.1 (default status for new incidents)
priority = critical from the policy matrix (impact high x urgency high); the request also calls it critical

disagreement: cells: B adds LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%switch%', A does not; chose A's cells because the request fixes no wording for the description (the issue is the connectivity drops; the switch is the CI, handled by the link and the work note) and the benchmark tests no short_description
category not tested: 'network issue' on a 'lab switch' could be read as network or hardware, and the request does not fix it
the incident table has no opened_by column; org_id is mandatory but unstated and not tested

requirements.text: the CI with serial number: NET-LAB-001 ... link this CI to the incident only if valid
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND configuration_item IS NULL
assumptions: NET-LAB-001 is CI_045 (IT Lab Switch), status = retired on the seed; policy 5.1 forbids linking retired CIs, so the link is not valid and must be absent
seed_count is 0 only because INC_101 does not exist on the seed; once created its configuration_item must be NULL
no other CI may be linked either: the request names only this serial (CI_004, the in-use Core-Switch-HQ, is a switch but not the lab switch), and no other serial on the seed is near NET-LAB-001

kind create: the cell is tested on the incident the task creates, which is absent on the seed, so the count goes from 0 to 1 once INC_101 exists with no CI; a stay would have to hold before the agent acts

requirements.text: link this CI to the incident only if valid
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101'
assumptions: the affected-CI related list is the other way to link a CI to an incident; the retired CI_045 may not be linked there either (policy 5.1)

disagreement: selector: A incident_id = 'INC_101' (no CI on the new incident), B configuration_item = 'CI_045' (CI_045 on no incident); chose A's because the request's object is the incident and it names one serial only, so any affected-CI row on INC_101 is unasked and the forbidden link (CI_045 to INC_101) falls inside it; CI_045 has no affected-CI row on the seed either way

requirements.text: Also audit the same in work notes
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND LOWER(worknotes) LIKE '%net-lab-001%' AND LOWER(worknotes) LIKE '%retired%' AND LOWER(worknotes) LIKE '%status%' AND LOWER(worknotes) LIKE '%not%' AND LOWER(worknotes) LIKE '%linked%'
assumptions: 'the same' read as the CI validation outcome: NET-LAB-001 is retired and was not linked
the five words (serial, retired, status, not, linked) are kept from the benchmark check; the request fixes no wording; case-insensitive as the check reads it

disagreement: kind: A create, B change; chose change because the cell is set by a later tool call on the created row (the audit follows the CI validation; update_incident is listed); seed_count is 0 because INC_101 does not exist yet

disagreement: cell form: A 'LIKE ...' on the column, B 'LOWER(worknotes) LIKE ...'; chose A's (a cell is a predicate on its column; the sql keeps LOWER() as the benchmark check writes it); same meaning
worknotes lives on the incident row (VARCHAR(120)); there is no separate work-note table in this schema

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the four requirements (INC_101 for David Ramirez at critical, its configuration_item left NULL, no affected-CI row, the work note with the benchmark's five words) and on all three dispositions; the differences are cells and forms, each logged in its requirement.
disagreement: incident cells: B adds short_description LIKE '%switch%', A does not; chose A's because the request fixes no wording and the benchmark tests no short_description.
disagreement: selector of the affected-CIs stay: A by the new incident, B by CI_045; chose A's because the request's object is the incident and it names one serial only.
disagreement: kind of the work-note requirement: A create, B change; chose change because the work note is set by a later update_incident call on the created row, after the CI is validated.
disagreement: cell form: B writes LOWER(worknotes) LIKE in the cells; chose the plain LIKE form on the column, the sql keeping LOWER() as the benchmark writes it.
The acting user Karen Watkins (USER_039) is an admin, so she may create the incident for the reporter David Ramirez (USER_018).
The CI check is the crux: NET-LAB-001 resolves to CI_045, status retired, which policy 5.1 says must not be linked; the incident is still created, with the refusal recorded in the work note.
INC_028 (closed) already links CI_045 on the seed through incident.configuration_item; that predates the task and is left to the collateral measurement.
Policy 7 asks for a knowledge search on incident creation; which articles match is undecidable and no listed tool searches or links knowledge, so neither pass wrote a requirement for it.
No requirement is a remove: nothing on the seed must be gone.
revised: the requirement that INC_101 has configuration_item NULL is a create, not a stay: INC_101 is absent on the seed (count 0) and the requirement needs the created row with no CI (count 1), whereas a stay must already hold before the agent acts; its sql and the benchmark check it carries are unchanged.
revised: the reason the work-note requirement is a change now stands on its own: the work note is written by a later update_incident call on the created row, after the CI is validated.
revised: notes set out one point per line, each disagreement on its own line.
